predictions.text: New Jersey Devils to win in New Jersey. The Devils are 6-4-0 through ten games, a .600 points rate, while Los Angeles arrive at 2-4-2 after eight games and have won only twice. New Jersey's twelve points from ten starts is double the Kings' six from eight, and the NHL's own published partner prices make New Jersey around -194, which sits with that gap. Goaltender confirmation and the injured list were not captured and are left blank.

Philadelphia 76ers to win. Philadelphia are 2-0 after two wins, with a 2-0 conference record and a 1-0 mark at home, while Milwaukee are 0-2, have lost two straight and are 0-2 against Eastern Conference opponents. Two games is a thin sample, so the edge is real but modest, and the price should not be treated as a mismatch. Injury reports for both rosters were not captured and remain blank.

Dallas Mavericks to win. Dallas are 1-1 and won their most recent game, while San Antonio are 0-2, have lost twice in a row and are 0-2 inside the Western Conference. The Spurs have also played both of their games at home, so this is their first road trip of the season. One game separates the two records, which keeps this a low-conviction call rather than a strong one.

The Pelicans are 0-1 in conference play and have not yet won. Because both teams have played one or two games, the records carry very little weight and this selection is the weakest on the card.
